links.outcome: Safety-critical omission rate with a downstream verification layer that modifies responses before return, versus guardrails alone
links.effect: Omission fell to the bare-model level (paired reduction 16.46 percentage points; 95% CI 10.93 to 21.86; P = 1.32e-23). The layer detected 49.0% of omissions the guardrails missed and missed none that the guardrails caught.
links.quote: A downstream verification layer that modified the response before it was returned lowered omission to the bare-model level (paired reduction 16.46 percentage points; Newcombe 95% confidence interval 10.93 to 21.86; McNemar exact P = 1.32 × 10⁻²³), detected 49.0% of the omissions the guardrails missed, and missed none that the guardrails caught (per-model 39.8% to 73.3%; P < 10⁻⁴).

links.outcome: Commission and safety-critical omission with a standard four-component guardrail stack versus bare model
links.effect: The guardrail stack lowered commission but raised safety-critical omission by 12.5 percentage points across 921 paired case-runs (17.6% to 30.1%).
links.quote: In a retrospective, pre-specified evaluation of three frontier large language models (GPT-5.5, Gemini 3.1 Pro, Claude Opus 4.7) on a contamination-excluded corpus of 1,363 clinical cases, a standard four-component guardrail stack lowered commission but raised safety-critical omission by 12.5 percentage points across 921 paired case-runs (17.6% to 30.1%).

unlisted_practices: Placement of the verification layer: acting on the response before return versus adding advisory text (advisory placement raised commission by 4.44 percentage points)
Assessing guardrails for omission of safety-critical care, not commission alone

screen.practice: downstream verification layer and standard guardrail stack
screen.reason: Empirical evaluation on a clinical benchmark testing the safety impact and trade-offs of standard guardrail stacks and downstream verification layers added to LLMs.
